title: Why I Started Building a Learning System
audience: Parents supporting a child through a difficult learning transition
sourcePerspective: I started building a reusable learning system after my child began struggling to keep up with math at a new school.

cards.headline: I started building a learning system.
cards.body: It began when my child started struggling to keep up with math at a new school.

cards.headline: The hardest part?
cards.body: My child still loved math—but keeping up with the pace became a real struggle.

cards.headline: As an engineer, I started with the root cause.
cards.body: I approached the problem the way I approach any difficult problem: find what is really getting in the way.

cards.headline: Then I broke it down.
cards.body: We identify the gaps and work through one piece at a time instead of treating everything as one big problem.

cards.headline: The system also had to be reusable.
cards.body: Time is limited, so I wanted a process we could return to—not something we had to rebuild every day.

cards.headline: Stay with us as we build, learn, and grow.
cards.body: This is the beginning of the system—and I’m looking forward to sharing what we learn along the way.

carousel.caption:
I started building a learning system when my child began struggling to keep up with math at a new school.

They still loved math. The challenge was finding the root cause, breaking it down, and creating a process we could actually reuse.

This is the beginning. Stay with us as we build, learn, and grow.
